scope: Individually owned source words retain their v1 drafts. A complete shared source pronunciation word can receive a v2 personal draft over all consecutive original PocketTorah member windows together, with no individual unit owner or inferred boundary.
identity: Original audio SHA1 and byte count
Independently measured PCM SHA256 and duration
Canonical reader word and reading occurrence
Exact marked reader Hebrew and original recording Hebrew
Selected source text style and row/column
Exact unit IDs, text, stress, original marks, written cluster ranges and shared-consonant underlay

For shared words: every canonical and occurrence ID, every exact marked member word, all separate original member windows, source reading choices, null individual owners and null pronunciation equivalence

annotations.start: Null until explicitly entered or captured; unchanged source seconds
annotations.end: Null until explicitly entered or captured; unchanged source seconds
annotations.constraints: Finite times within the independently checked original word window, with positive complete intervals and source order preserved even across blank units. No gaps, neighbors, phonemes or musical notes are inferred. Captured clock values are not rounded across a source boundary.

independence: Sephardic and Ashkenazic are source transcription styles, separate from Kinnor’s six historical Accent labels. Each style, source variant and reading occurrence has a separate draft. Changing text does not change the original recording’s pronunciation, musical source, instrument key, range or BPM. Preview uses the unchanged source at original pitch/speed, without changing main practice preferences.
sourceLimitations: Shared source words are available only as complete groups with consecutive, exactly touching original windows in one duration-checked recording. Missing or unreliable windows, gaps, overlaps, reordered members, changed marked Hebrew and windows outside measured audio fail closed; no boundary is clipped, shifted or invented. Source-only reading forms keep null written ranges. Source-edition/recorded-pronunciation equivalence remains unreviewed.
storage: Personal localStorage drafts keyed by source audio identity, canonical word, occurrence, text style and source variant. Prepared JSON/download is cleared on edits, imports and context changes. Import validates against a freshly constructed source identity. No draft can certify its own phonemes, notes, source-edition comparison or independent review. Shared-group keys retain the ordered canonical/member occurrence lists and source choices. V1 individual drafts keep their original keys and data format. Boundary input immediately clears an old prepared export. Leaving a field, preparing or auditioning validates both pending boundaries atomically before saving; unchanged captured values retain their original clock basis.
playback: Explicit Play original word or Audition draft syllable uses the existing source player and source checksum checks. Reference/chant volume applies. Zero volume runs a muted clock with the media paused, and its captures remain labeled muted-clock. Instrumental and processed source practice cannot supply captures. Stop and the existing hidden-tab stop apply. Shared-word previews have no individual word or syllable clock: the complete original interval, or an explicitly entered personal subinterval, is played with an empty word-follow list. Both original word clocks remain separately recorded in the draft. Text style, instrumental tempo, transpose and range do not change the recording or its preview rate.

requiredToReplaceDrafts: A qualified reader must compare the exact source edition and actual recorded pronunciation with each selected source transcription variant.

A qualified annotator must identify audible syllable and phoneme boundaries in the matching original recording, with explicit uncertainty and independent review; clock captures alone do not prove them.

Reusable sung-phone recordings or a reviewed synthesis voice, complete source-based phonological specifications for each historical pronunciation, and contextual note/duration/F0 realization are still needed for independent sung styles.
